title: Disconnects, timeouts, and partial-delta flush protocol for streamed responses
creator: Jordan Lee
description:
Problem: When clients disconnect or hit timeouts during long-running streamed generations (chat/structured outputs / tool calls), the server currently drops in-flight state and may leave partial tokens in caches or produce incomplete structured fragments which are hard for callers to reconcile. This impacts customer SLAs (partial outputs counted as failed generations), leads to stale KV cache entries, and creates surprising behaviors for older SDKs that lack resume semantics.

Goals:
- Define a server-side protocol to safely flush partial deltas and snapshot generation progress on disconnects/timeouts.
- Provide resume tokens (opaque IDs) and short-lived "quarantine" windows so clients can reconnect and resume with minimal wasted compute.
- Ensure KV cache hygiene (invalidate or mark entries) to avoid stale cache reuse after aborted generations.
- Provide compatibility fallback for older SDKs and 3rd-party integrations that only expect final outputs.
- Add clear observability (metrics, traces) for aborted/resumed generation flows.

Constraints and non-goals:
- We will not change model checkpointing internals; the approach must sit at the runtime/serving layer.
- Resume tokens are short-lived (configurable, default 30s) and do not create long-term storage requirements.
- This ticket does not implement full multi-region resume; that is a follow-up.

Proposed approach (high level):
1) Delta flush + Snapshot: on graceful client disconnect or request timeout, the runtime writes a delta snapshot of the last committed tokens and metadata (sequence length, KV cache fingerprint) into an ephemeral resume store. Snapshot includes a checksum and a resume_token (UUID).
2) Quarantine window: snapshot lives for X seconds (configurable; default 30s) during which resumed requests referencing the token may pick up where the generation left off. If no resume happens, snapshot is garbage-collected and any KV cache associated with the aborted generation is invalidated or downgraded to avoid reuse.
3) Resume semantics: SDKs can call the existing streaming endpoint with "resume_token" and a resume-mode header. Server validates token, checks KV fingerprint compatibility, and either resumes (fast-path) or returns a 409 with hints (incompatible) so caller can re-request fresh generation.
4) Partial structured output repair: for structured JSON outputs, server attempts a best-effort reparse of the last delta and emits a Repair hint event in the stream (structured-output/repair) so higher-level tooling can stitch partial payloads.
5) Compatibility layer: default behavior when client provides no resume_token is unchanged. We add an opt-in server flag to enable the protocol per-tenant to avoid surprising behavior for existing customers. For legacy SDKs, provide a shim in console docs showing how to convert partial fragments to complete results.

Acceptance criteria:
- Streaming runtime writes snapshot on client disconnect and serves resume requests within quarantine window.
- KV cache entries tied to aborted snapshots are either invalidated or marked as low-confidence to avoid future pollution.
- New metrics: streaming.aborts, streaming.resumes, streaming.resume_latency, streaming.partial_repair_count.
- SDK integration tests for resume success, resume-incompatible, and GC behavior.
- Performance: no >5% tail-latency regression under baseline steady-state traffic.

Rollout plan:
- Feature gated behind tenant opt-in + runtime flag.
- Canary rollout to small set of internal tenants for 2 weeks.
- Gradual ramp with observability thresholds (error spikes or >1% resume failures triggers rollback).

Notes on trade-offs:
- Storing snapshots increases memory/ephemeral storage usage; we limit snapshot size (max last 1k tokens) and TTL to bound cost.
- Aggressive GC reduces resume success rate but lowers memory pressure; default TTL 30s chosen after perf simulation.
- Compatibility fallbacks add logic complexity; we keep old behavior as default to avoid breaking customers.

Resources / references:

- RFC: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1Dd_resume_protocol_rfc

comments: 2026-03-10 Jordan Lee: Initial ticket created after postmortem from INC-2026-03-08 (customer observed repeated 499s during long tool-calls). Proposed TTL 30s based on early perf runs.

2026-03-11 Aisha Kumar: Spike implemented local prototype. Confirmed resume fast-path reduces duplicate token generation by ~82% in lab. Prototype PR opened: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1456
2026-03-11 Mike Patel (review): Concern about KV cache fingerprints being brittle across quantization variants. Suggest storing model-version + architecture fingerprint alongside KV hash.

2026-03-12 Priya Nair (security): Reviewed resume_token lifecycle, recommended making tokens HMAC-signed by KMS and short TTL to avoid replay attacks. Marked security_review_required=false for now but follow-up to integrate KMS required before GA.

2026-03-12 Design review (Lena Ortiz): For structured JSON repair events, designers prefer emitting an explicit 'repair_advice' structure that client UX can display instead of raw fragments. Added to acceptance criteria.

2026-03-13 Aisha Kumar: Implemented snapshot GC and KV invalidation flag. Running chaos tests with deliberate client disconnects using loadgen-2026-03. Results posted in the dashboard link in resources.
2026-03-13 QA (Evan Cho): Added test cases for legacy SDKs that simply close connection; ensure server does not keep snapshots by default for older tenants.
test_plan: Unit tests for snapshot creation/consumption, integration tests for resume token verification, chaos testing with simulated disconnects (loadgen), compatibility tests against v1 SDKs. Add metrics and automated alert rules to detect resume failures.
implementation_notes: Key code areas: streaming controller (snapshot writer), ephemeral resume store (in-memory + bounded disk), resume validation layer, KV cache metadata tagging. Keep snapshot max size at 1k tokens and TTL default 30s. Add API header: X-Resume-Token and Resume-Mode. Emit structured event 'partial_repair' on structured outputs.
follow_up: Multi-region resume support (ENG-22011), GA KMS-signed tokens (ENG-21980), SDK updates and examples (ENG-21845), add tenant-configurable TTL via console (PM-402).
notes_for_support: When customers report truncated outputs: ask for request_id + timestamp. Check streaming.aborts and streaming.resume_* metrics. If resume_token present, check resume validity and KV fingerprint mismatches in logs.
